propositions: An autouse caplog containment guard exists for the root 'rebar' logger but does not cover the sibling 'rebar_reconciler' root, leaving INFO assertions in later tests vulnerable to leaked WARNING-level constraints from earlier reconciler-entrypoint tests.

When a test drives the reconciler entrypoint in-process, logging.getLogger('rebar_reconciler').setLevel(logging.WARNING) is called process-globally and never restored, poisoning all later tests in the same xdist worker.

caplog.at_level(logging.INFO) without a logger= argument raises only the ROOT logger level, so INFO records from intermediate loggers like rebar_reconciler are dropped by isEnabledFor before reaching caplog's handler, while WARNING records still propagate.

test_pass_summary_reports_the_decline_count fails deterministically when run after test_main_entry.py with -p no:randomly, because the per-item WARNING is captured but the pass-summary INFO is dropped at the originating logger.

The fix generalizes tests/_log_integrity.py primitives from scalar REBAR_LOGGER_NAME to tuple SHARED_LOGGER_NAMES and updates the conftest autouse guard to snapshot and restore the level of both roots.

When confirm_store is None, the removal is applied (not declined), so declined==0 and missing summary are correct-by-design; the per-item WARNING presence in captures proves confirm_store was non-None, ruling out the storeless path hypothesis.
